notes.summary: Alligation is a quick way to find the ratio in which two things at different prices (or strengths) must be mixed to get a given mean. 0–2 questions in SSC.

concepts.title: Rule of alligation
concepts.body: Cheaper : Dearer = (Dearer − Mean) : (Mean − Cheaper). Works for prices, percentages, speeds, profits — any weighted average of two groups.

concepts.title: Replacement
concepts.body: If x litres are taken out of V litres of pure liquid and replaced with water, n times, the pure liquid left = V(1 − x/V)n.

varieties.name: Alligation ratio
varieties.how: Write the two values and the mean; cross-subtract to get the ratio.

example.q: In what ratio must tea at ₹ 60/kg be mixed with tea at ₹ 75/kg to get tea worth ₹ 70/kg?
A 40 L can of milk: 4 L is replaced with water once. Milk left?

varieties.name: Adding to a mixture
varieties.how: Keep the quantity that does not change fixed and adjust the other.

example.q: 20 L mixture has milk : water = 3 : 1. How much water to add to make it 3 : 2?

tips: Water has cost 0 in price-based alligation.
When mixing two mixtures in equal quantity, average the fractions of each component.
traps: Keep the order: the ratio (Dearer − Mean) belongs to the CHEAPER item.
In replacement, the formula gives the quantity left, not the quantity removed.

questions.q: Rice at ₹ 20 per kg is mixed with rice at ₹ 25 per kg to get a mixture worth ₹ 22 per kg. In what ratio are they mixed?
A 60-litre mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 2 : 1. How much water must be added to make the ratio 1 : 2?
questions.solution:
Milk = 40 L, water = 20 L.
For milk : water = 1 : 2, water must be 80 L.
Water to add = 80 − 20 = 60 L.

questions.q: A vessel contains 80 litres of pure milk. 8 litres are taken out and replaced with water. This is done once more. How much milk is now in the vessel?
In what ratio must water be mixed with milk costing ₹ 60 per litre to get a mixture worth ₹ 50 per litre?
Two vessels contain milk and water in the ratios 3 : 1 and 5 : 3. If equal quantities from both vessels are mixed, what is the ratio of milk to water in the new mixture?
questions.solution:
Milk fraction: 3/4 in the first, 5/8 in the second.
Take 8 L of each: milk = 6 + 5 = 11, water = 2 + 3 = 5.
Ratio = 11 : 5.

questions.q: A merchant has 1000 kg of sugar. He sells a part at 8% profit and the rest at 18% profit, gaining 14% overall. How much sugar did he sell at 18% profit?
